subject.title: refactor(plugin-sdk): narrow wildcard barrels to explicit used exports

question: Does the round-5 directive intentionally authorize removing shipped Plugin SDK symbols in a minor release based only on observed corpus usage, despite the documented deprecation and major-release policy?
rationale: The implementation can be repaired mechanically, but choosing whether corpus observation may redefine the supported public contract is an SDK product-policy decision that automation should not infer.

options.title: Honor compatibility policy
options.body: Retain the shipped symbols, add explicit deprecation records and migration guidance, and defer removal until the approved window or major release.

options.title: Approve an intentional break
options.body: Explicitly authorize the minor-release contract break, document affected entrypoints and migration replacements, and accept unknown third-party plugin failures.

options.title: Narrow internal surfaces only
options.body: Land internal star-export cleanup and dead-code removal now while deferring all public symbol removals to a dedicated compatibility change.

recommendation.title: Honor compatibility policy
recommendation.body: Retain the shipped symbols, add explicit deprecation records and migration guidance, and defer removal until the approved window or major release.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged precursor and this branch show direct ownership of the current SDK contract-reduction program.
